next_step: Finalize SLO language around p50/p95/p99 for streaming and non-streaming; run 72h synthetic with client SDK instrumentation
blockers: final egress throughput numbers from network team
notes:
Highgate is a merchant payments platform evaluating Redwood Dedicated for deterministic latency during high-volume settlement windows. CTO told AE on 2026-03-12: "We require clear client-observed p99 for checkout flows and separate guarantees for streaming chat first-byte and per-token cadence."

SE shorthand:
- Client insists primary KPI = SDK-measured end-to-end latency (send -> first-byte for sync; send -> first-token and median token interval for streaming).
- Needs p50/p95/p99 defined and how aggregated (rolling 1h windows vs calendar-day).
- Peak: ~9k concurrent checkout validations during 8-9am ET; avg payload 220 tokens. Nightly RAG and batch reconciliations.
- Wants reserved GPU count with documented burst pool and autoscale thresholds.
- Security: VPC peering + customer-managed KMS; SOC2 evidence and 12-month audit log retention requested.
timeline: 2025-10-05 - Lead created from integration partner intro (AE Samir)
2026-01-18 - Hosted API PoC; functional fit but inconsistent p99 under peak
2026-02-05 - Intro capacity sizing workshop; initial ask 10-14 GPUs for peak
2026-03-01 - SDK traces sample provided by customer
2026-03-12 - SLO alignment call; agreed to draft explicit measurement plan
use_case_summary: Primary: synchronous checkout fraud/risk validation requiring deterministic p99. Secondary: reranking for fraud signals. Support chat uses streaming for agent assist; UX-sensitive to first-byte and steady token emit rate. RAG for transaction history retrieval nightly.
requirements_summary: Hard SLOs: synchronous checkout p50/p95/p99 targets with client-perceived p99 <= 450ms. Streaming chat: p95 first-byte <= 180ms, p99 token-emit interval <= 35ms (target >= 28 tokens/sec steady-state). Must run in customer VPC, keys in customer KMS, audit logs for 12 months, US data residency. Throughput: sustain 9k concurrent checkout requests at 220 tokens average during peak.
sla_preferences: Prefer calendar-month reporting window. Requests 99.9% uptime SLA for Dedicated with business-hours tougher targets (M-F 6am-8pm ET). Wants explicit SLO aggregation windows, documented fallback model behavior, and definition of burst-credit consumption and replenishment.
measurement_alignment_plan: Define terminology: 'client-perceived latency' = SDK timestamp send_time -> first_byte_time for sync flows; for streaming define t_fb (first-byte), t_emit_median, t_emit_p99, and t_completion
Specify aggregation windows: rolling 1h for operational alerts, calendar-day for monthly SLO accounting; calculate p50/p95/p99 on valid samples only
Instrument both sides: require SDK to emit send_time and first_byte_time (UTC ms), Redwood to emit arrival_ts, queue_wait_ms, infer_ms, emit_ms for correlation
Establish trust hierarchy: 1) customer SDK traces (primary for credits), 2) Redwood server telemetry (secondary), 3) infra provider metrics (auditing)

Streaming rules: SLOs applied to first-byte (p95) and per-token cadence (p99). Define how long-tail long responses are bucketed (exclude responses >60s from median token-rate SLO but include in completion SLO)
Synthetic validation: 72h run using customer network profile (latency jitter, packet loss) and real prompt length distribution to validate reserved GPU sizing, batching config, and KV cache hit rates
Sampling & exclusions: require minimum 5k valid samples/day for p99; exclude client-network incidents explicitly flagged by SDK tracer; define reconciliation steps if SDK vs server p99 diverge >10%
Operational cadence: daily health dashboard during first 14 days post-cutover, weekly SLA sync for first 60 days, monthly thereafter
